acceptanceCriteria: Confirm or refute with a deterministic test: cancel the dispatcher after admitProgress saves a ledger without the ended, progress-granted workers, but before `finish` performs final accounting.
If confirmed, the accounting is either made durable before the workers leave the ledger, or recovered on the next open, so no ended worker's escalation accounting is lost.
The governing spec (corvint-tasks dispatch/user-service) names the behaviour and the test witnesses it.
body:
Pre-existing, suspected defect, found 2026-10-05 during the V1-0697 / #500 fix round (branch claude/v1-0697-fence-drain at ad54459d, clone /private/tmp/claude-501/corvint-v1-0697-r2). Codex review P2-2 first named it. The V1-0697 fix stops it from settling a drain early: settlement now happens only at the end of a completed, uncancelled tick. The underlying accounting loss is out of that slice's scope.

Scenario: admitProgress removes ended workers that already have progress and saves that ledger. Then a stop, SIGTERM or context cancel arrives before `finish` does the final accounting (the cancel check near internal/tasks/dispatch/loop.go:467). That tick's escalation accounting is never applied, and no retained worker is left to retry it.

Expected: every ended worker's accounting is applied exactly once, even across an interrupt. Actual (suspected): it can be dropped.

Related, but not the same: V1-0672 (a dispatcher tick silently ignores a failed private ledger save) and V1-0697.
